events.title: Initial Cardiology Consultation
findings: Patient presented with exertional dyspnea and mild bilateral pedal edema for 3 weeks
Blood pressure elevated at 148/92 mmHg, Heart rate 84 bpm
Normal S1/S2 with faint systolic ejection murmur at base
events.sourceSnippet: Chief Complaint: 58-year-old female presenting with progressive shortness of breath on exertion and lower extremity swelling. Plan: Start Lisinopril 10mg PO daily, order Echocardiogram and basic metabolic panel.

events.title: Transthoracic Echocardiogram & Blood Panel
findings: Left Ventricular Ejection Fraction (LVEF) preserved at 55-60%
Mild concentric left ventricular hypertrophy
Serum Creatinine 0.9 mg/dL, eGFR >60 mL/min/1.73m² (within normal limits)
BNP slightly elevated at 165 pg/mL (ref <100 pg/mL)
events.sourceSnippet: Impression: LVEF estimated at 58% with grade 1 diastolic dysfunction and mild concentric LVH. BNP mildly elevated at 165 pg/mL.

events.title: Outpatient Follow-up & Medication Adjustment
findings: Significant resolution of dyspnea and pedal edema
Blood pressure well controlled at 124/78 mmHg
Patient tolerating ACE inhibitor therapy without dry cough
medications: Hydrochlorothiazide 12.5mg PO daily added for optimal fluid balance
events.sourceSnippet: Patient reports marked improvement in exercise tolerance. BP 124/78. Recommend continuing Lisinopril 10mg and adding low-dose HCTZ 12.5mg.
